title: Console: SCM Cost Breakdown UI Notes (field mapping, copy, mock payloads)
content:
Last updated: 2025-03-04 (Marissa + Console eng sync)

Goal
- Document how Console’s Cost Breakdown page maps Standard Cost Model (SCM) API fields -> UI sections.
- Capture copy/UX decisions for “estimated”, “assumptions”, and “confidence”.
- Provide mock payloads used by frontend + backend integration while staging is unstable.

Audience
- Console backend + UI: Dylan / Chloe / Jada
- Platform SCM service: Priya / Jordan
- Support enablement (later): Felix

Scope for initial Console release (SCM v1)
- Read-only display of estimated technical cost + breakdown.
- NOT used for invoice/billing (explicit label in UI).
- Works across Hosted + Dedicated; Private later (same fields, may have more missing signals).

Terminology (for UI copy + tooltips)
- “Estimated cost”: cost computed by SCM using runtime + catalog signals and documented assumptions.
- “Metered attribution”: when telemetry provides enough data to attribute costs post-hoc; may differ from estimate; not displayed in v1 UI (keep as internal debug in “Details”).
- “Assumptions”: explicit statements about missing/approximated inputs (e.g., cache hit rate unknown -> default).
- “Confidence”: 0..1 number + band label. UI shows band label; numeric shown only in Debug.

High-level UX
Page: Console > Usage > Cost Breakdown (per time range, per model/route filter)
Sections (top to bottom):
1) Summary card
2) Breakdown table (by component)
3) Drivers (batching, caching, quant profile, prefill/decode split)
4) Assumptions & confidence
5) Details (debug, expandable)

Key UI constraints
- Must be legible for non-infra users: show “what changed” + drivers.
- Must be safe under missing/partial data: render assumptions, don’t silently show $0.
- Must not imply billing truth: include “For transparency; not your invoice” language.
- Need consistent units across pages: USD, per 1K tokens, and total over selected range.

API endpoints (as used by Console)
- /v{X}/scm/estimate (preferred for “what would this cost?” and for historical aggregates w/ missing telemetry)
- /v{X}/scm/explain (preferred when we have request-level or route-level detailed signals)

Console calling pattern (UI level)
- Summary/breakdown: use explain when available; fall back to estimate if explain returns UNSUPPORTED_MODE or missing required signals.
- Cache results for the time-range + filters (backend)
- If SCM times out -> show breakdown unavailable state + keep overall Usage numbers (don’t block page)

Field mapping (SCM -> UI)

A) Summary card
- UI label: “Estimated inference cost”
  - SCM: total_cost.value
  - SCM: total_cost.currency (expected: "USD")
- Secondary metrics (small text)
  - “Requests”: from Console usage pipeline (not SCM)
  - “Input tokens / Output tokens”: from token metering (Console)
  - “Avg cost / 1K tokens”: computed client-side using total tokens (Console) and total_cost

Copy (summary)
- Header tooltip:
  "Estimated technical cost based on runtime telemetry and documented assumptions. This is not your invoice amount."
- Inline note when confidence != high:
  "Estimate has reduced confidence due to missing telemetry signals. See assumptions."

B) Breakdown table
We need consistent component names that are stable even if SCM adds new components later.

Recommended visible rows (v1)
1) GPU compute
  - SCM: breakdown.components[].id == "gpu_compute"
  - Display name: "GPU compute"
2) GPU memory / KV-cache
  - SCM: id == "gpu_memory"
  - Display name: "GPU memory"
3) Networking / overhead
  - SCM: id == "network_overhead" (or "platform_overhead" if that’s what SCM settles on; confirm)
  - Display name: "Platform overhead"
4) Cache impact (savings)
  - SCM: id == "cache_savings" (negative value)
  - Display name: "Caching savings"

Notes
- If a component is missing, do not render the row.
- If a component value is negative (savings), render with leading minus and “savings” label.
- Always show total row at bottom: equals total_cost.

Table columns
- Component (name + tooltip)
- Cost (USD)
- Share (% of total_cost; for negative values show "—" or allow negative share? Proposed: show absolute share in gray + "(savings)"; final TBD.)

Component tooltips (draft)
- GPU compute: "Compute time spent generating tokens (prefill + decode) adjusted for batching efficiency."
- GPU memory: "Memory footprint and KV-cache overhead attributable to this workload."
- Platform overhead: "Non-model overhead (request routing, serialization, safety checks), estimated."
- Caching savings: "Estimated reduction in compute due to cache hits."

C) Drivers section (qualitative “why is this high/low?”)
The driver cards are derived primarily from explain.* fields.

Drivers we want (v1)
1) Batching
- SCM: factors.batching.batch_size_effective (number)
- SCM: factors.batching.efficiency (0..1 or percent)
- UI copy:
  - "Batching" card shows:
    - "Effective batch size: X"
    - "Efficiency: Y%"
  - Tooltip: "Higher batching efficiency lowers cost per token, but may increase latency."

2) Caching
- SCM: factors.caching.kv_cache_hit_rate (0..1)
- SCM: factors.caching.cache_mode ("cold" | "warm" | "unknown")
- UI copy:
  - "KV-cache hit rate: Z%" (or "Unknown")
  - Secondary: "Cache state: Warm/Cold" if provided

3) Prefill vs decode
- SCM: factors.tokens.prefill_tokens
- SCM: factors.tokens.decode_tokens
- UI: stacked bar or two-line ratio (don’t overdo in v1)
- Tooltip: "Prefill is processing input tokens; decode is generating output tokens. Longer inputs increase prefill cost."

4) Quantization profile
- SCM: factors.model.quant_profile_id
- SCM: factors.model.quant_profile_label (if provided)
- SCM: factors.model.quantization_bits (if provided)
- UI copy:
  - "Quantization: <label>" e.g., "INT8", "FP16", "NF4"
  - Tooltip: "Quantization can reduce cost but may affect quality. Optimize recommendations may suggest alternatives."

Driver display rules
- If factor values missing: show “—” and move details into Assumptions.
- If factors present but confidence low: show a subtle warning under Drivers (“Some drivers are estimated”).

D) Assumptions & confidence section
This is a dedicated section; avoid burying in tooltips.

Confidence display
- SCM: confidence.score (0..1)
- SCM: confidence.band ("high" | "medium" | "low")
- UI:
  - Title: "Confidence"
  - Pill: High / Medium / Low
  - Subtitle:
    - High: "Based on complete telemetry for this selection."
    - Medium: "Based on partial telemetry; some values are estimated."
    - Low: "Based on limited telemetry; treat as directional."

Assumptions list
- SCM: assumptions[] (array of strings or structured; if structured, backend should join to strings for UI)
- UI renders bullet list with optional “Learn more” link (internal doc / FAQ).

Copy guidance (do not scare users)
- Use neutral language: “estimated using defaults” instead of “missing/unknown/bad data”.
- If we had to default region/SKU: explicitly mention it.
- Avoid mentioning internal metric names in the non-debug view.

Example assumptions (copy-ready)
- "KV-cache hit rate not available for part of the selected time range; estimate assumes 0% cache hits."
- "GPU SKU was inferred from deployment configuration; estimate assumes H100-80GB equivalent pricing baseline."
- "Batching efficiency not reported for some requests; estimate uses median efficiency for this model in this region."

E) Details (debug, expandable)
Intended for power users + support.

Show (collapsed by default)
- SCM version used
  - SCM: scm_version (e.g., "1.0")
- Request metadata (for explain)
  - request_id / trace_id if present (do not show for aggregated views)
- Normalization + SKU
  - region
  - gpu_sku
  - pricing_basis / cost_basis_id (if SCM emits)
- Full raw JSON payload (behind “Copy JSON” button)

Privacy note
- Do not display tenant_id, internal actor ids, or any PII.
- If raw payload contains internal ids, backend must redact before returning to UI.

States / error handling

Loading
- Skeleton for Summary + Breakdown

SCM unavailable (timeout/5xx)
- Keep page usable; show inline panel:
  Title: "Cost breakdown temporarily unavailable"
  Body: "We couldn’t load the cost breakdown right now. Usage metrics are still available. Try again in a few minutes."
  Actions: [Retry]

SCM validation error (4xx)
- Usually indicates bug/mismatch between Console query -> SCM required inputs.
- Show a different message (more actionable for internal users; but this is customer-facing page, so keep generic):
  Title: "Cost breakdown unavailable for this selection"
  Body: "This breakdown requires additional telemetry that isn’t available for the current filters/time range."
  Link (internal only / feature-flagged): “View error details” (shows error code + request id)

Low confidence (not an error)
- Render normally but include the confidence pill + assumptions section expanded by default.

Aggregation notes (Console time range)
- Console often asks for aggregate over a range; SCM explain may be request-scoped.
- Current approach for v1 Console:
  - For time-range aggregate breakdown: SCM returns “aggregate_explain” payload (sum across sampled/aggregated telemetry) OR Console calls SCM per-route bucket (e.g., per model+region) and sums.
  - Backend should own summation to keep determinism.
- UI should not show per-request trace details in aggregate mode.

Mock payloads

Mock #1: Explain payload (single route aggregate) – HIGH confidence
{
  "scm_version": "1.0",
  "mode": "explain",
  "scope": "aggregate",
  "time_range": "2025-02-24T00:00:00Z..2025-02-24T01:00:00Z",
  "filters": "route=/v1/chat/completions model=redwood-llama-70b region=us-east-1",
  "total_cost": {"value": 12.4831, "currency": "USD"},
  "breakdown": {
    "components": [
      {"id": "gpu_compute", "label": "GPU compute", "value": 9.7740, "currency": "USD"},
      {"id": "gpu_memory", "label": "GPU memory", "value": 2.1063, "currency": "USD"},
      {"id": "platform_overhead", "label": "Platform overhead", "value": 0.8428, "currency": "USD"},
      {"id": "cache_savings", "label": "Caching savings", "value": -0.2400, "currency": "USD"}
    ]
  },
  "factors": {
    "tokens": {"prefill_tokens": 1850000, "decode_tokens": 920000, "total_tokens": 2770000},
    "batching": {"batch_size_effective": 7.2, "efficiency": 0.81},
    "caching": {"kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.12, "cache_mode": "warm"},
    "model": {"model_id": "redwood-llama-70b", "quant_profile_id": "qp_fp16_default", "quant_profile_label": "FP16"},
    "infra": {"region": "us-east-1", "gpu_sku": "H100-80GB"}
  },
  "assumptions": [
    "Platform overhead is estimated using a fixed per-request baseline for this route.",
    "Cache savings estimated from KV-cache hit rate telemetry aggregated at 1-minute resolution."
  ],
  "confidence": {"score": 0.93, "band": "high"}
}

Mock #2: Explain payload – LOW confidence (missing caching + batching signals)
{
  "scm_version": "1.0",
  "mode": "explain",
  "scope": "aggregate",
  "time_range": "2025-02-20T00:00:00Z..2025-02-20T06:00:00Z",
  "filters": "route=/v1/embeddings model=redwood-embed-3 region=eu-west-1",
  "total_cost": {"value": 1.9075, "currency": "USD"},
  "breakdown": {
    "components": [
      {"id": "gpu_compute", "label": "GPU compute", "value": 1.7121, "currency": "USD"},
      {"id": "gpu_memory", "label": "GPU memory", "value": 0.1642, "currency": "USD"},
      {"id": "platform_overhead", "label": "Platform overhead", "value": 0.0312, "currency": "USD"}
    ]
  },
  "factors": {
    "tokens": {"prefill_tokens": 0, "decode_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0},
    "batching": {"batch_size_effective": null, "efficiency": null},
    "caching": {"kv_cache_hit_rate": null, "cache_mode": "unknown"},
    "model": {"model_id": "redwood-embed-3", "quant_profile_id": "qp_int8_fast", "quant_profile_label": "INT8"},
    "infra": {"region": "eu-west-1", "gpu_sku": "L40S"}
  },
  "assumptions": [
    "Token counts are not available for this route in the selected time range; estimate is based on average request size for this model.",
    "Batching telemetry missing; estimate assumes median batching efficiency for this model/region.",
    "KV-cache hit rate not available; estimate assumes 0% cache hits."
  ],
  "confidence": {"score": 0.41, "band": "low"}
}

Mock #3: Error payload (for internal debug)
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    "message": "region is required",
    "request_id": "scmreq_01JMD0Z8Q1QK8MZB3E..."
  }
}

UI copy notes (draft language)
- Page title: “Cost breakdown”
- Subtitle: “Estimated technical cost for inference (not invoice)”
- Section headers:
  - “Summary” (optional; might be redundant)
  - “Breakdown”
  - “Cost drivers”
  - “Assumptions & confidence”
  - “Details”

Open questions / TODO
1) Component naming stability
- Confirm canonical IDs in SCM v1 spec: gpu_compute, gpu_memory, platform_overhead/network_overhead, cache_savings.
- Action: Jordan to confirm final component IDs; Console will map unknown IDs to a generic row (“Other”).

2) Negative values display
- Decide whether to allow negative shares in breakdown.
- Proposal: show savings as negative USD but omit percent share to avoid confusion.

3) Confidence score semantics
- Confirm whether confidence.score is linear and comparable across models/regions or only internal ranking.
- UI will display band only until we’re confident.

4) Private deployment gaps
- Expect more missing signals; ensure the assumptions list doesn’t become too long.
- Potential: cap displayed assumptions to 5 + “and X more” link.

5) Support enablement
- We need an internal FAQ for Support: “Why breakdown != invoice?”, “Why did caching savings disappear?”, etc.
- Action: Felix to draft with Marissa once wording finalized.

6) Performance / payload size
- explain payload can get big if we add too many factors.
- Ask SCM service to keep factor sets bounded (no per-layer stats, no per-request list in aggregate).

Notes from 2025-03-01 copy review (Marissa email thread)
- Avoid “accuracy” claims. Prefer “confidence” + “assumptions”.
- Always show “estimated” in the UI (don’t toggle away even if high confidence).
- If customers ask: point them to assumptions section and offer “export JSON” (later) for deeper debugging.
